findings.text: Exposes lock-free read helpers for versioned clock data. Callers capture a start version, read payload, then validate that the version did not change. One variant signals time namespace contention instead of spinning. All helpers are tiny inline routines suitable for vDSO use.

Exposes writer helpers that invalidate a clock version before mutation and revalidate it after, with ordering between version and payload. Single clock and dual clock forms exist, with the dual form covering coarse high resolution and raw clocks together.

Exposes fixed width multiply helpers. One widens two 32 bit factors to 64 bits. The other combines a 64 bit value with a 32 bit factor plus a 64 bit addend, then shifts right, with two evaluations that preserve carry and high half contributions.
Exposes type generic unaligned accessors that transfer a value between memory and a local through a size matched byte copy, avoiding alignment assumptions for both load and store directions.

Odd version means a writer is active. Readers wait while odd, apply acquire ordering once even, and fail validation if the closing version differs. Writers advance to odd before changing payload and to even after, with release ordering separating version changes from payload and with untorn version stores.

Time data updates invalidate and revalidate the coarse and raw clocks as a pair, with one ordering barrier between invalidation and payload mutation on entry and between payload completion and revalidation on exit.

A clock counts as time namespace only when namespace support is enabled and its mode field indicates that mode. The namespace aware reader reports contention when it observes an odd version on such a clock rather than waiting.

Vector affinity construction honours caller reservations at both ends, defaults to a single set when no sizing callback is supplied, spreads middle vectors evenly across present CPUs per set, gives reserved edge vectors default affinity, and marks the middle range managed. Absence of assignable vectors, oversize set counts, or allocation failure yields a null result.

Vector total computation adds reservations to the smaller of available vectors and either caller addressable vectors or possible CPU weight depending on whether a set sizing callback exists, and reports zero when reservations exceed the requested minimum.

Managed startup clears any prior managed shutdown indication, proceeds normally when the line is not managed, aborts with shutdown marked when no online CPU intersects affinity, warns when abort is forced, and activates reserved resources before reporting managed success. An alternate configuration always reports the normal path.

Startup resets nesting depth, reenables already started lines, otherwise selects managed handling and then either programs affinity before or after chip startup depending on chip flags for normal lines or programs supplied affinity before chip startup for managed lines. A resend request is honoured after successful startup.

Affinity programming requires a chip handler, narrows managed requests using housekeeping and online sets unless forced, records the requested mask on success codes that permit copy, validates effective affinity, wakes threaded handlers needing reaffinity, defers through a pending mask when movement cannot happen in process context or is already pending, schedules notification when registered, and records that affinity was set.

Hierarchical activation walks to the parent before invoking local activation and rolls back the parent when local activation fails, marking success only once. Deactivation invokes local teardown then recurses to the parent. A simplified configuration marks activated and succeeds without hierarchy traversal.
Effective affinity validation is configuration dependent. One form warns once when the effective mask remains empty after programming, identifying chip and line. The other form performs no check.
Descriptor lookup is configuration dependent. One form loads from a sparse tree by number. The other indexes a flat table when the number is below the maximum and otherwise yields null.
Autoprobing serializes with a dedicated mutex held across the whole detection sequence, while each descriptor scan holds that descriptor spinlock with interrupts disabled.
Public affinity changes resolve the descriptor then hold its spinlock with interrupts saved while applying the locked update path.
Versioned clock data uses no sleepable lock. Readers and writers coordinate through odd even versioning plus acquire ordering after version capture and release ordering around payload mutation.
Time namespace offset carries seconds as signed 64 bit followed by nanoseconds as unsigned 64 bit.

Legacy 32 bit time uses a signed 32 bit seconds alias. Both legacy timestamp and legacy interval pair that seconds field with a signed 32 bit subsecond field, nanoseconds for the timestamp and microseconds for the interval.

Decimal time scales are fixed. A second contains one thousand milliseconds, one million microseconds, one billion nanoseconds, one trillion picoseconds and one quadrillion femtoseconds. A millisecond contains one thousand microseconds and one million nanoseconds. A microsecond contains one thousand nanoseconds.

Fixed width limits derive from all ones patterns. Unsigned maxima are bitwise negation of zero in the respective width, signed maxima shift that pattern right by one, signed minima negate the maxima and subtract one, and pointer maximum aliases the unsigned long maximum.

Page geometry derives from a configured shift. Size is one shifted by that amount and mask is the negated size minus one, with an alternate mask spelling using shift directly. Tick length rounds seconds per second divided by ticks per second to nearest, and low resolution duration aliases tick length.
Shared vDSO data symbols alias update base and time data base to the same link location derived from page count and page size, extended with random and architecture specific reservations.

Chip lines move among disabled, masked and started indications. Enable clears disabled then either invokes chip enable and clears masked or unmasks. Unmask only acts when masked is set and clears it after chip unmask. Chip startup clears both disabled and masked and then sets started.

Probe candidates move from idle to armed with autodetect plus waiting, to spurious when waiting clears before sampling and then disarmed, to pending when activation fails, with only surviving low numbered lines reported in the result mask.

Interrupt state lives in a common field reached through one accessor. Helpers set or clear started, disabled, masked, activated, affinity set, move pending and managed shutdown indications without disturbing other bits.
Probe entry quiesces asynchronous work and returns a bit mask of low numbered lines that remained silent through staged activation and filtering, holding serialization for the whole operation.
Affinity construction entries create per vector descriptors from vector counts plus reservation and sizing inputs, and compute feasible vector totals from minima, maxima and possible CPU weight.
Affinity setting entries accept a line number plus CPU mask with optional forcing, resolve and lock the descriptor, then apply immediate or deferred programming with notification.
Chip lifecycle entries activate then force start a line, start or reenable a line with optional resend, and unmask a masked line through the chip handler.
Domain entries activate a hierarchical line exactly once with parent first ordering and rollback, and tear it down parent last.

Affinity and startup paths fail safely. Null follows oversize or allocation failure, zero vectors follow reservations exceeding minima, invalid argument follows absent chip programming or no online CPU match without forcing, and abort with managed shutdown follows affinity lacking online CPUs.

Probing tolerates longstanding and spurious activity through staged waits, reactivation, and filtering before reporting, while effective affinity programming warns when the chip leaves the effective mask empty.
Each small vDSO and time header defines a distinct inclusion guard macro that prevents repeated inclusion within one translation unit.
